title: Enchanting
summary: Bind SkyRPG enchants at the Arcane Enchanting screen, use tomes, combine and salvage them, and fill the Codex.

s.x: SkyRPG replaces vanilla's enchanting table with its own enchants: 72 of them, from simple stat boosts to effects like lightning and cheating death. You bind them at
Arcane Enchanting
, find them as
tomes
, and every bind levels the
Enchanting
skill. This page covers how it all works. The full enchant list is on
Enchant list
. Vanilla enchanted books from loot and the anvil still work as before.
Seraphine Vael
, the Enchanter in the tower in the hub. Her library counts as 15 bookshelves, and you can stay within 12 blocks of her.
Any enchanting table.
Right-click it to open the same screen. Stay within 8 blocks of the table.
A table's
power
is the number of bookshelves around it (vanilla's rule: two blocks out, with air between), up to 15. Higher enchant levels need power:
A table only offers up to level V. Higher levels (some enchants go to VI or VII) only come from tomes.
A violet window with an altar in the middle: two rune rings turn against each other and light bursts when something is bound. It has three tabs.
Enchant:

your enchantable gear on the left (worn armour first, then the held item, hotbar, bag and offhand), the item on the altar with what it already holds, and the enchants the table offers for it on the right. Pick an enchant and a level, then
Bind
. Locked levels say why (bookshelves, or your Enchanting level).
Tomes:
your tomes on the left. For the chosen tome you can
Combine
it with an identical one,
Salvage
it into Runic Dust, or
Apply
it to any item you carry that takes it. Each row shows the change, for example "II to Keen III", and the cost.
Codex:

every enchant there is, filtered by weapons, bows, armour, tools, fishing and ultimates, with what each does at its highest level and where it comes from. Hover for every level and the conflicts. Tome-only enchants you have not seen yet show as runes.
Replacing something (a conflicting enchant, or another ultimate) needs a second click. The footer shows your coins, XP levels, Lapis, Runic Dust and Enchanting level.

Each enchant goes on a kind of item: swords, bows and crossbows, armour (any piece or one slot), pickaxes, axes, hoes, any tool, fishing rods or wands. Only single items can be enchanted, never a stack. Armour enchants work in their own slot, and everything else works while held in your main hand. An item with enchants glints.
Conflicts:
Keen, Hallowed Edge and Webcutter exclude each other.
Ultimates:
an item holds only one ultimate.
An enchant costs coins, XP levels, Lapis and, for the rarer ones, Runic Dust and Prism Fragments. Each level is paid in full, not as a difference. Materials are taken from your backpacks too.

s.x: Reseeding has its own price (4,000 coins, 8 XP levels, Enchanting 5, 12 Lapis and 16 Dewdrops).
A tome is an item that holds one enchant at one level. Apply it at the screen to put that enchant on an item.
Applying

gives the tome's level if it is higher than the item's. A tome of the same level as the item's raises it by one, up to the enchant's maximum. It costs coins (300 for Common up to 25,000 for an Ultimate, times the level it ends at) and 3 XP levels per level.
Combining

two identical tomes (same enchant, same level) makes one a level higher. This is the only way past the table's level V. It costs coins (150 to 10,000 times the new level squared) and, from Uncommon up, Runic Dust.
Salvaging
a tome gives
Runic Dust
: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 or 40 by rarity (Common to Ultimate), doubled for every level above I. Runic Dust sells for 80 coins, but the best binds and merges ask for it.
Hostile mobs:
about 0.5% per kill, a little more for tougher mobs (up to 2%), times Magic Find and the Tome Hunter talent. They are combat enchants of levels I to III, mostly Common. Spawner mobs never drop them.
Gathering:

while you gain XP in a skill, there is a small chance of a tome for that skill's gear: mining 0.06%, foraging 0.06%, farming 0.04%, fishing 1% per catch. The skill's ultimate is much rarer (mining and foraging 0.003%, farming 0.002%, fishing 0.06%).
Slayer bosses and the world boss:
each drops its own enchants (and a small chance of
Unbreakable
), with a higher tier giving better odds.
Dungeon bosses and champions:
each dungeon boss and champion has its own tome drops.

At the table:
Enchanting level 22: 150,000 coins, 30 XP levels, 48 Lapis and 32 Runic Dust.
As a tome:
a rare drop from the world boss (4%) and from the slayer bosses at tier III (1.5%) and tier IV (3%).
It does nothing on weapons, armour, shields, bows or accessories, which never wear in the first place.
Upgrading the tool at the Artisan Bench keeps it.
An ultimate is the top enchant for its slot, and an item holds only one. They come as tomes only.

s.x: Most enchants give stats (they show up as the "Enchants" source on your Stats page), and the rest switch on effects such as life steal, thorns, dodging, replanting or double drops. Extra hits from enchants are magic damage and never set off other enchants.
Enchanting is a skill with 50 levels on the same curve as the others. Each level gives +1 Intelligence and +0.2 Magic Find. It also gates the higher enchant levels (see the cost table).

s.x: The Codex records every enchant you have had on an item in your bag or as a tome. The first time you find one you get a chat line, a "CODEX DISCOVERY" banner and the XP above. Your bags are checked every five seconds.
Chase first discoveries early. An Ultimate tome in your bag is worth 5,000 Enchanting XP the moment the Codex notices it, even before you use it.
